paper_title: Computational Intractability of Strategizing against Online Learners
authors: Angelos Assos, Yuval Dagan, Nived Rajaraman
statement: structure, as was extensively studied in prior literature. It remains open what is the best runtime for the optimizer. While it is not polynomial in the game size unless P = NP, can it be polynomial in 𝑇? Can the runtime depend exponentially only on min(|𝒜|, |ℬ|)? Concretely, is there an algorithm that runs in time poly(|𝒜|, |ℬ|, 𝑇)𝑒 𝑂(min(|𝒜|,|ℬ|)) ? Further, beyond the special cases studied, is there a broader class of games in which it is possible to efficiently find optimize the optimizer’s reward? Beyond MWU, there is an efficient optimization algorithm against no-swap regret learners (Deng et al., 2019b), but what about other learners? Taking the learner’s perspective, can one analyze how well it performs against optimizers and which learning algorithms are desired in such a scenario? See related work for some studies in this direction.
